definition: Logic Programming Associates (LPA) is a company specializing in logic programming and artificial intelligence software.
details: LPA was founded in 1980 and is widely known for its range of Prolog compilers, the Flex expert system toolkit and most recently, VisiRule. LPA was established to exploit research at the Department of Computing and Control at Imperial College London into logic programming carried out under the supervision of Prof Robert Kowalski.

explainer.lead: Logic Programming Associates is a company specialising in logic programming and AI software, founded in 1980. It matters as a long-standing vendor of Prolog tooling and rule-based expert system kits.

tiers.eli5: It is a small firm that builds tools for writing rules a computer can reason with, rather than just calculate.
tiers.practitioner: Developers use its Prolog compilers and the Flex expert system toolkit, and more recently VisiRule, to build rule-based systems. A caveat is that such toolchains are specialised, so teams need logic-programming skills rather than general software experience alone.
tiers.paperLevel: The company was established to exploit research at the Department of Computing and Control at Imperial College London into logic programming carried out under the supervision of Prof Robert Kowalski. Its products target logic programming and expert system development specifically.

explainer.example: A team encodes eligibility policy as Prolog rules using an LPA compiler so the rules can be queried and revised without rewriting application code.
